Task: Establish a trustworthy Mos Aster performance baseline

Goal

Within 120 minutes, produce a reproducible, full-quality performance baseline on the M2 MacBook Air, supported by usable Xcode/Instruments evidence. Identify one measured cost worth investigating next, or specify the exact additional measurement needed when attribution remains inconclusive.

This phase establishes evidence. It does not optimize gameplay or require achieving 60 FPS.

Branch and starting point

Create an isolated worktree and new branch:

codex/mos-aster-perf-phase-1-baseline

Start from:

057f52ecbad7e4d33047004b09ad1ed68bafe1c5

This is the reviewed codex/mos-aster-racing-city baseline. Use codex/mos-aster-performance-experiments only as historical reference.

Read AGENTS.md, docs/simulator-agent-rules.md, docs/apple-gpu-profiling.md, and docs/renderer-study.md before work.

Verify target hardware and tooling during the first 15 minutes. If the M2 or necessary tooling is unavailable, report the specific blocker; M4 results cannot complete this task.

Scope

Preserve production geometry, audio, population, effects, detail, native 1920×1080 drawable dimensions, 2× MSAA, AO, and both existing shadow maps.

Minimal diagnostic or reporting changes are permitted when necessary. Keep them out of normal gameplay. Use existing tools first; a comprehensive presentation-importer rewrite is outside this phase.

At this baseline, run-sustained-performance.py has no --presentation option, and read-game-overview.py is diagnostic-only. Inspect their actual capabilities before using them.

Work

1. Build the release app. Record commit, binary hash, asset identity, hardware, OS/Xcode versions, audio output configuration, quality settings, and relevant environment overrides.
2. Run separate clean ten-minute clear and storm town-driving baselines with controlled starting conditions. Record native cadence, update timing, thermal history, and available resource counters.
3. Record one matching clear run with Game Performance Overview plus Points of Interest. Check process/layer identity, drawable dimensions, benchmark UUID, start/end markers, and measured-window coverage.
4. Obtain short matched early/loaded Metal System Traces and one usable Xcode GPU capture. Confirm they finalize and export. Inspect expensive passes/draws and available CPU samples. Keep capture timings separate from clean-run measurements.
5. Analyze the evidence. Rank thermal limits, accumulating work, and resource pressure as hypotheses; do not claim causation from correlation.
6. Select one narrowly scoped next experiment, stating its measured target, expected mechanism, comparison method, and preservation checks.

A failed performance gate is useful baseline evidence. Distinguish it from failed collection or invalid profiling evidence.

Time allocation

- 0–20 min: setup, build, provenance and quality verification
- 20–55 min: clean clear/storm runs
- 55–85 min: presentation recording and export
- 85–105 min: short detailed captures and inspection
- 105–120 min: analysis and handoff

Defer repeat runs, dedicated Audio System Trace, or extensive tooling repairs when they cannot fit. Stop at 120 minutes and report outstanding work honestly.

Deliverables

Save a report and compact machine-readable summaries under:

docs/performance-validation/<run-date>/phase-1-baseline/

Keep large raw traces outside Git, referenced by path and hash. Include exact reproduction commands and the branch commit with appropriate Entire provenance.

Definition of done

Phase 1 is complete when:

- Both clean weather runs cover 600 measured seconds at verified production settings.
- Results include per-minute cadence, P95/P99/worst intervals, gaps above 25 ms, worst rolling ten-second cadence, CPU update timing, and thermal history.
- At least one finalized Apple presentation trace covers the measured window; identity and coverage checks are documented, with unresolved limitations explicit.
- Short Metal evidence and a usable GPU capture support at least one concrete rendering-cost observation.
- Callback cadence, actual presentation, GPU elapsed envelopes, and exclusive GPU busy time are clearly distinguished.
- The report chooses one actionable next experiment—or an exact discriminating capture where diagnosis remains inconclusive.
- Production behavior and quality remain unchanged.

Missing mandatory evidence means partial or blocked, not completed. A slow baseline can still satisfy the task: the goal is trustworthy evidence and a justified next step.

I’ll verify the M2 hardware and profiling tools first, then create the isolated worktree and inspect the benchmark scripts. I’ll keep capture overhead separate from the clean runs and report any missing evidence as partial or blocked within the two-hour limit.
